newsitem.title: USA: Brooke denounces tobacco pact in letter.
newsitem.headline: Brooke denounces tobacco pact in letter.

text.p: Brooke Group Ltd Chairman Bennett LeBow on Wednesday sharply criticized last week's historic $368.5 billion tobacco pact, lashing out against state officials involved in the deal.

"Not only have you breached your contractual agreements and your moral obligations, but the way you have conducted yourselves does serious damage to the public interest," LeBow wrote in a letter to attorneys general of 25 states.
Brooke Group, whose Liggett tobacco unit makes brands such as Chesterfield and Lark, stunned the industry in March by striking settlements with states that had sued the industry.

On Monday, Brooke Group attorney Marc Kasowtiz told Reuters that the settlement struck on Friday would bankrupt Liggett and did not include protections that had been set under its own accord. LeBow's letter reiterated those concerns.

In the Liggett settlement, the company agreed to pay states 25 percent of its pretax profits for the next 25 years in return for immunity from lawsuits. It also agreed to turn over internal tobacco documents.
In the letter, LeBow described Liggett as "the whistleblower that will forever change the way the tobacco industry does business."
"This deal punishes Liggett, the one tobacco company that has brought everyone else to the table," he wrote.
